BiblicalUsage: The abnet is the embroidered sash or girdle — part of the priest’s garments and the royal official’s dress. It is listed among Aaron’s holy garments, woven of fine linen and needlework; and Moses girds Aaron with it at the consecration.
TheologicalSignificance: A sash sounds small, but it is the piece that holds the garments together and marks the man as set apart for service — a picture of readiness, of a priest girded for work.
